subject: gov.policy
name: ANSUT strategic plan 2026-2030
milestone: Unveiled by the agency’s director general 2026-08-11
position_end: Built on four pillars — universal connectivity, digital services and financial inclusion, digital usage and literacy, and operational excellence — across ten projects, four of them funded at FCFA 60.144bn through the national development plan and six from the agency’s own funds; the stated targets are 300 newly connected localities, smartphone penetration of 80% by 2028 against 40% now, and more than 15,000 km of new fibre by 2028, against a starting point of 70% of rural households with no internet access
note: no adoption instrument published; the plan is the agency’s own

subject: gov.policy
name: Education digitalisation strategy 2024-2028
milestone: Issued for the period 2024-2028
position_start: The national strategy for the digitalisation of education in Cote d'Ivoire, running 2024-2028
position_end: The national strategy for the digitalisation of education in Cote d'Ivoire, running 2024-2028
note: the strategy document carries no adoption instrument

subject: gov.policy
name: Information system master plan of the economy ministry
milestone: Adopted and presented December 2025
position_end: Adopted at FCFA 10.156bn across six programmes and 44 projects, after a diagnostic found weak IT governance, non-interconnected platforms, ageing infrastructure and insufficient security
note: nothing on file since adoption on what has been built

subject: gov.policy
name: National Cybersecurity Strategy 2021-2025
milestone: Evaluation presented at the Abidjan-Plateau workshop 2026-07-23
position_end: Expired and evaluated, and still the text formally in force because no successor has been adopted
note: the reported completion split is not established from any held document

subject: gov.policy
name: National Cybersecurity Strategy 2026-2030
milestone: Draft presented for stakeholder review 2026-07-23, awaiting the Council of Ministers
position_end: Draft held as a PDF on five axes, extending scope to artificial intelligence, emerging technologies and cloud and adding results-based monitoring
note: the held PDF has not been text-extracted, so its structure remains a press claim

subject: gov.legislate
name: Any Ivorian artificial-intelligence statute
milestone: No instrument published
position_end: None published; governance runs entirely through non-binding strategy instruments, with the draft cybersecurity strategy the only binding-track vehicle extending state scope to artificial intelligence
note: a published bill, act or implementing decree would settle it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Loi n 2013-546 on electronic transactions
milestone: Article 50 repealed by ordinance, ratified 2025
position_end: In force; its 2014 and 2016 implementing decrees on cryptology, electronic signature and digital archiving are the stated legal basis of the national public key infrastructure
note: the only Ivorian digital statute the base can name implementing decrees for

subject: gov.legislate
name: Loi n 2024-352 on electronic communications
milestone: Annual compliance seminar reviewing its application, April 2026
position_end: In force, with 2025 operator compliance action plans evaluated, licence terms under revision and a common conformity framework being defined
note: first appears in the base in 2026; no text held

subject: gov.legislate
name: National cyber-security agency
milestone: Created by decree October 2024, launched 2025-02-11
position_start: Agency launched and consolidating the cybercrime unit, the national computer emergency team and the alert line
position_end: Operating agency running a national security operations centre, a public-administration security-officer network, the national public key infrastructure and auditor certification against the state security reference framework

subject: gov.legislate
name: Ordonnance n 2024-950 transferring the cyber mandate
milestone: Ratified by the Senate 2025-06-16
position_start: Ratified, moving network security, audit, certification and electronic-certificate issuance from the telecoms regulator to the cyber agency
position_end: Unchanged in law; the transferred certificate mandate is now exercised through the national public key infrastructure

subject: gov.legislate
name: Procedure for handling consumer complaints on electronic communications
milestone: Harmonised procedure validated by the regulator, 2026-08-26
position_end: The regulator has validated a harmonised procedure for handling consumer complaints against operators and internet service providers, now to be transmitted to its Conseil de regulation for possible adoption
note: no draft text, adoption date or redress standard is published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Regulatory Council of the telecoms authority
milestone: Sworn in 2026-05-07, installed 2026-05-11
position_start: Outgoing council, whose mandate took more than a thousand sector decisions
position_end: New six-year council installed, with a roadmap of priorities handed to the minister

subject: gov.protect
name: Compliance and authorisation caseload
milestone: About a hundred physical files a month at the compliance platform's launch
position_end: About 100 physical data-protection compliance files handled per month immediately before the platform went live
note: no post-launch throughput figure has been published

subject: gov.protect
name: Loi n 2013-450 on personal data protection
milestone: Since 19 June 2013
position_start: In force, with the telecoms regulator designated the data-protection authority
position_end: In force and unamended, with the regulator confirmed as the authority after the cyber agency's creation; no separable data-protection appropriation exists
note: the base holds no text of the law and no implementing decree

subject: gov.protect
name: Register of data-protection officers
milestone: Created in 2026 per the minister's stocktake
position_end: Created and named by the minister alongside simplified norms as one of the country's data-protection advances
note: no register size, publication or legal basis is stated

subject: gov.protect
name: Regulator annual activity report
milestone: 2024 edition not located across two automated attempts
position_end: No 2024 or 2025 edition published on the regulator's site; the most recent locatable report anywhere is 2022
note: publication of the 2024 report would settle it, and is the only route to whether the data-protection function has a separable budget

subject: gov.protect
name: Regulator position on mobile-money agent identity copies
milestone: The agents' union wrote to the regulator 2026-07-24; no answer on file
position_end: Four questions put to the regulator on whether kiosk agents may demand, photograph or retain customer identity documents; no response on file as at 2026-08-05
note: a regulator communique or decision would settle it

subject: gov.standards
name: ECOWAS migration and macroeconomic data harmonisation
milestone: Two regional workshops held at Abidjan 18-22 August 2026
position_end: Two regional statistics workshops convened at Abidjan on 18-22 August 2026 under the ECOWAS Commission's research and statistics directorate and the PHASAOC harmonisation project - the sixth Regional Coordination Meeting, which reviewed and validated the third edition of the Regional Report on International Migration in West Africa, and a capacity-building session for national committees on compiling macroeconomic statistics for the Convergence and Macroeconomic Stability Pact - taking up updates to the ECOMAC and ECOBASE databases and harmonisation of national series for 2000-2025
note: a regional programme hosted in the country; no Ivorian national migration-data strategy is on file

subject: gov.standards
name: General interoperability framework for information systems
milestone: Adopted by decret n 2021-913 of 22 December 2021
position_start: Adopted by decret n 2021-913 of 22 December 2021 as the general reference framework for interoperability of information systems
position_end: Adopted by decret n 2021-913 of 22 December 2021 as the general reference framework for interoperability of information systems
note: the operating platform built to it is carried on a separate row

subject: gov.standards
name: Migration data governance strategy
milestone: Named by the diaspora directorate at the 30 July 2026 profiling workshop
position_end: Named as the framework for a fourteen-body returning-migrant profiling instrument, and the subject of a regional ECOWAS meeting hosted at Abidjan in August 2026, but nothing establishes it exists as a published document
note: a reference number or adoption decree would settle it. Abidjan hosted an ECOWAS regional meeting on migration data and international mobility on 2026-08-18, which is the second occasion in three weeks on which the national strategy has been referred to without being produced

subject: gov.standards
name: State security reference framework auditor certification
milestone: 88 auditors certified at an Abidjan-Plateau ceremony
position_end: Auditor certification running, with 88 certified and a further certification announced for experts bringing information systems into conformity
note: the reference framework's own text is not held

subject: gov.discourse
name: Consumer grievance platform
milestone: Launched in Abidjan 2026-07-30
position_end: Live application and web platform at FCFA 150 per report, with eight stages from filing through mediation to published reports and sectoral dashboards
note: a consumer association rather than a regulator holds the national grievance dataset, and charges for entry

subject: gov.discourse
name: Online gendered violence against election candidates
position_end: Documented as cyclical across successive elections in a two-country civil-society study, with no state measurement held against it
note: a civil-society research organisation's study of online gendered violence against candidates across election cycles in Côte d'Ivoire and Tanzania; the base holds no regulator, electoral-commission or platform figure for the same phenomenon, so this is the only measurement of it on file and it is the researcher's own

subject: finance.budget
name: Digital ministry appropriation
milestone: FY2026 finance law promulgated 2025-12-19
position_start: FCFA 60,780,440,826 voted for FY2025, no outturn
position_end: FCFA 83,275,503,595 voted for FY2026, up 37%, no outturn
note: the press figure is exactly the four budget lines summed

subject: finance.budget
name: FY2024 digital budget execution
milestone: FY2024 settlement law execution column
position_start: None published, the settlement law not yet voted

subject: finance.budget
name: Levy share of the digital ministry vote
milestone: FY2026 finance law
position_start: 65.6% of the ministry's section was earmarked operator levy in FY2025
position_end: 42.7% for FY2026, as the ministry's own programme rises from FCFA 19.03bn to 45.99bn while both levy programmes shrink
note: the ratio is the wiki's own compilation of the four budget lines, not a figure any source states

subject: finance.budget
name: Published accounts of the universal service fund
milestone: No account of the levy's use is on file
position_end: No account of the levy collected or spent is published; the state portfolio report is the nearest published financial statement, recording the agency at FCFA 7.9bn of tax receipts in 2023, the largest single contributor in its segment, inside a group of seven non-commercial bodies whose net results fell by a cumulative FCFA 19.8bn
note: the agency publishes no annual report; the settlement law for 2025, due December 2026, would settle the outturn

subject: finance.budget
name: Telecoms regulation levy programme
milestone: FY2026 finance law
position_end: FCFA 2,580,000,000 appropriated for FY2026, down 43.8%
note: the regulator has published no annual report for 2024, so the levy has no public account of what it bought

subject: finance.budget
name: Universal service levy programme
milestone: FY2026 finance law promulgated 2025-12-19
position_start: FCFA 35,300,000,000 appropriated for FY2025, no outturn published
position_end: FCFA 33,000,000,000 appropriated for FY2026, the programme renamed, still no outturn
note: the only outturn on file is FY2024, FCFA 32.30bn voted against FCFA 24.44bn executed, a 24.3% shortfall

subject: finance.budget
name: Whole-of-government digital appropriation
milestone: FY2026 finance law
position_start: FCFA 82,227,745,121 across 20 lines for FY2025, no outturn
position_end: FCFA 104,342,019,358 across 20 lines for FY2026
note: the roll-up is the wiki's own compilation of 61 line-years across six ministries

subject: finance.mou
name: Five-year telecommunications and digital-infrastructure memorandum with an Indian technology company
milestone: Dated 2026-08-07 and fully executed 2026-08-19
position_end: A five-year memorandum of agreement between an Indian technology company, a continental investment council and an Ivorian mobile operator to develop telecommunications and digital public infrastructure across the continent, dated 2026-08-07 and fully executed on 2026-08-19 per a regulatory filing. It covers national fibre backbones, 4G and 5G, submarine cable landing stations, internet exchange points, telecom towers, and digital identity, national interoperability, e-government and digital payment platforms. No financial commitment is disclosed
note: known only from the company's regulatory filing; no country programme, project, site or value is named

subject: finance.new
name: CDC-CI Capital startup seed programme
milestone: US$1.2m injected into Ivorian ventures, May 2026
position_end: The state deposit fund's investment arm extended its startup funding with a US$1.2m injection into Ivorian ventures in May 2026 under a 2026 seed programme, against a wider startup surge the sector press dates to April 2026

subject: finance.new
name: Cybastion digital infrastructure programme
milestone: Government authorisation reported 2026-08-10
position_end: The government has authorised a United States technology firm to carry out a set of projects strengthening national digital infrastructure, the whole estimated at US$170m, about FCFA 95bn
note: no signed contract, financing instrument, component list, timetable or procurement route is held for the programme

subject: finance.new
name: Non-state digital finance stock
milestone: Compiled from the deal records the wiki holds
position_end: US$1.29bn across 24 deals from 2018 to 2026
note: the roll-up is the wiki's own compilation, not a source figure, and two loans may be one filed twice

subject: finance.new
name: World Bank inclusive digitalisation programme
milestone: Loan agreement ratified by decree at the Conseil des ministres 2026-02-04
position_start: Procurement plan covering September 2023 to December 2024 across four components, with no financing agreement concluded
position_end: Phase 1 financed by an IDA credit of FCFA 84,356,070,200 (EUR 128.6m) concluded 2025-10-17 and ratified 2026-02-04, inside a US$330m multiphase envelope running to 2035; Phase 1 is fenced to Abidjan, Yamoussoukro and twelve regions, and allocates US$45m to broadband for public institutions and US$50m to legal and institutional foundations
note: the FY2024 finance law records the programme at zero appropriated and FCFA 500,000,000 executed, a line opened in-year

subject: infra.connect
name: 2Africa Ivory Coast branch
milestone: Restored to service 2026-08-02 after an outage
position_end: All services live after repair; WACS repairs expected the following week
note: the outage's start date, cause and duration are not stated

subject: infra.connect
name: 5G commercial launch
status: Implemented, on provisional spectrum pending a definitive award
milestone: Provisional frequency allocation granted 19 December 2023, service opened for the 2024 Cup of Nations
position_start: Spectrum re-planned and financial terms settled after a missed 2023 target, with the regulator calling deployment imminent
position_end: Service has run on re-allocated existing frequencies since a provisional allocation of 19 December 2023, which let the two largest operators offer 5G for the Cup of Nations in January and February 2024, reaching 7 per cent of the population in 2025 and used first for fixed broadband where there is no fibre; the definitive award and the commercial launch announced for July 2026 remain undelivered
note: The provisional allocation and the definitive award are different things: the base recorded the second as stalled and had no record of the first, which an industry survey has now supplied.

subject: infra.connect
name: CIVIX national internet exchange point
milestone: Average daily traffic put at 36 Gbps
position_start: Operating; a memorandum signed June 2025 to colocate a third point of presence at a Grand-Bassam facility
position_end: Operating with Netflix and Akamai peering alongside operators and ISPs at 36 Gbps daily average
note: nothing on file confirms the third point of presence was commissioned

subject: infra.connect
name: Deployed optical fibre
milestone: Ministry stated roughly 38,000 km
position_end: About 38,000 km, with connectivity reaching nearly one million homes; the state broadband backbone accounts for over 6,600 km
note: a third figure of over 33,000 km for 2024 is in tension with the 2025 count

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile coverage and internet users
milestone: Ministry stated 95% coverage and nearly 15m users
position_start: 4G covering 73.34% of localities and 93.71% of the population; the universal-service agency put territorial coverage at 82%
position_end: 95% mobile coverage, telecom penetration above 130% of population, nearly 15m active internet users and about 2m e-commerce users; smartphone adoption 41%
note: coverage figures switch between territory, localities and population without a stated base

subject: infra.connect
name: MTN satellite broadband
milestone: Partnership announced April 2026
position_end: Hybrid geostationary and low-orbit capacity aimed at rural white areas; no subscriber, price or coverage figure on file

subject: infra.connect
name: National IPv6 migration strategy
milestone: Draft strategy and action plan validated at Yamoussoukro
position_start: Strategy and action plan validated with about twenty public and private bodies; IPv6 penetration 6.6%
position_end: Unchanged; no adoption, no publication and no later penetration figure on file as at 2026-08-05
note: the second attempt, after a first roadmap in 2013

subject: infra.connect
name: National strategy to protect electronic-communications infrastructure
milestone: First national assises held at Grand-Bassam
position_end: Operators, infrastructure managers and the regulator working towards a protection strategy after 665 acts of theft and vandalism nationally between January and October 2025; no instrument published

subject: infra.connect
name: Orange Sat satellite broadband
milestone: Launched January 2026
position_end: Satellite broadband sold by the incumbent into rural white areas on leased geostationary capacity; no subscriber, price or coverage figure on file

subject: infra.connect
name: Predictive fibre-cut sensing
milestone: Proof of concept completed in Abidjan, reported 2026-08-13
position_end: An operator and its vendor completed a proof of concept in Abidjan detecting vibrations around fibre ducts and classifying them to flag third-party excavation before a cut happens, on long-term trials run since 2025; no commercial deployment, coverage or date is stated
note: the account is vendor-issued

subject: infra.connect
name: Programme national de connectivite rurale

position_end: US$68m stated for connecting 575 rural localities
note: the figure and the locality count are the ministry's own as reported; no completion date, disbursement or connected-locality count is published

subject: infra.connect
name: RASCOM capacity in universal coverage
milestone: Ministry visit to the regional satellite body, 2026-07-31
position_end: Government has chosen satellite for areas terrestrial infrastructure serves poorly and intends to route regional satellite capacity through the universal-service bodies; no terms, tariff or timetable stated
note: the only satellite route here that is not a foreign operator selling into white areas

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink Network CIV

position_end: Selling nationally on a 12-month provisional licence reviewable on service quality, hardware XOF 148,148 to 247,466 and service from XOF 28,746 a month
note: the definitive individual licence under the 2024 electronic communications law is not yet issued

subject: infra.connect
name: Via Africa submarine cable
milestone: Consortium memorandum signed
position_end: Europe-to-South Africa Atlantic system with an Ivorian landing; route survey funded and supplier selection being prepared, with no landing date, capacity or cost stated
note: the held Ivorian account is a reprint of the consortium release

subject: infra.store

position_end: No launch, capacity, pricing or customer on file as at 2026-08-05
note: the only AI-compute hosting claim the base holds for this country

subject: infra.store
name: National Data Centre
milestone: Formal authorisation to proceed at US$170m
position_start: Sovereign data centre at the core of the digital city project, construction reported begun May 2025, no financing figure held
position_end: US$170m US export-credit-financed project formally authorised, scope now a sovereign national data centre, a government digitisation platform and a smart-border surveillance system; no site, capacity or completion date stated
note: financing rose from US$66m approved August 2025 to US$170m authorised July 2026

subject: infra.store
name: Raxio CIV1, VITIB Grand-Bassam

position_start: Tier III carrier-neutral facility operating since September 2024, with a June 2025 memorandum with the state on hosting government workloads

subject: infra.store
name: Tier III data centre, VITIB Grand-Bassam
milestone: Inaugurated 2025-10-02

subject: infra.energy
name: Electricity load of data centres and telecom sites
milestone: No measured load published; one facility's design figure is all that is held
position_end: No measured load, efficiency ratio, generator arrangement or utility tariff is published for any Ivorian facility; the only figure disclosed is a design capacity of about 400 racks and 1.5 MW of IT power for the Grand-Bassam carrier-neutral facility, from its 2022 environmental study
note: an operator disclosure or a utility connection agreement would settle it

subject: infra.cybersec

subject: infra.cybersec

note: a government self-report; the platform's caseload is the separate national cybercrime report row, which is Not held

subject: infra.cybersec

milestone: FY2026 finance law voted
position_start: FCFA 3.268bn for modernising and securing the treasury information system and FCFA 791.9m for the budget information system, FY2025
position_end: FCFA 1.618bn for the treasury system, roughly halved, against FCFA 841.9m for the budget system, FY2026
note: the only separable cyber-security appropriations identifiable in the Ivorian budget

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National cybercrime report

position_start: The 2024 report presented 2025-05-22, recording 12,100 complaints, FCFA 6,960,903,038 of loss and 338 arrests
position_end: The 2024 edition is now held as the agency's own document rather than at second hand; no 2025 edition is on file and the most recent national cybercrime figures are more than eighteen months old
note: an agency report for 2025 would settle it

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National public key infrastructure
milestone: Commissioning announced 2026-07-23
position_start: The root certification centre was listed as one of the state agency's technical units, with no national root of trust in service
position_end: Sovereign national root at the head of the internationally recognised certificate tree and trust anchor for every certification authority operating in the country, under the 2013 electronic transactions law and its 2014 and 2016 decrees

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Reseau national des RSSI

subject: infra.cybersec

subject: dpi.exchange

name: Digital post box
milestone: Made obligatory from 2026-03-01
position_end: Compulsory for all individuals and businesses with postal addresses and tied to the identification number, at annual fees from FCFA 2,000 for an individual to 50,000 for a large business
note: no count of boxes assigned, and no account of enforcement after the March deadline

subject: dpi.id
name: Holders of the national identification number
milestone: Figure given by the identification office's director general
position_end: Roughly 11 million, in a substantially larger population
note: relayed through a commentary piece, not established from an official publication, and carrying no as-of date

subject: dpi.id
name: MaPoste application
milestone: Launched January 2026
position_end: Register-backed application for mail and parcel management, identity-card, birth-certificate and criminal-record applications, with card delivery through more than 200 post offices
note: no download, registration or transaction figure published since launch

subject: dpi.id
name: National biometric register and identification number
milestone: In operation throughout the window
position_start: Biometric register issuing the national identification number, coverage not published
position_end: Same, with historic duplicate identities inside the register now named publicly by the identification office's director general
note: what moved in the year is disclosure, not the register

subject: dpi.id
name: Population identification appropriation
milestone: Voted identically in the 2026 finance law
position_end: FCFA 8,791,576,615 for FY2026, unchanged, up from FCFA 5,000,000,000 in FY2024
note: the largest single named digital line in the Ivorian state budget

subject: dpi.id
name: Register authentication service for banks
milestone: Convention signed 2025-11-11
position_end: One bank integrated for real-time identity checks against the national register
note: no second bank appears on file as at 2026-08-05, and no pricing is stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cross-network mobile-money transfer app
milestone: Launched May 2026
position_end: Private app moving funds directly between mobile-money networks, live in six West African countries with instant cross-border transfers
note: volumes, licensing and regulatory status are not stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: e-impots online tax declaration and payment portal
milestone: Opened by the tax directorate January 2017
position_end: More than 74,000 registered taxpayers as at 15 March 2022, the portal carrying over 22% of the tax directorate's collected revenue in its first year of operation and more than 78% in 2021
note: no figure on file since March 2022

subject: dpi.pay
name: Fourth electronic-money licence
milestone: Licence granted 2025-09
position_end: Four, with a locally built wallet issued by the new licensee
note: a later account names a fifth operator among electronic-money institutions, which this count does not include

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile-money accounts and transaction volume
milestone: Central bank annual report on digital financial services, data to 2024-12-31
position_start: 13,441,990 mobile-money subscribers moving FCFA 8,236bn a year (2018 market statistics, the regulator's last published)
position_end: 99,649,204 electronic-money accounts opened at 2024-12-31, 40.07% of the monetary union's total and the largest share in it, of which 26,370,627 active (26.46%); 2,549,268,326 transactions, 21.4% of the union's volume and 34.7% of its value; merchant acceptance points up from 1,131,590 to 2,719,463 in the year
note: the two ends are on different definitions, mobile-money subscribers against electronic-money accounts opened

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile-money agent surcharge
milestone: Levied on every counter transaction since November 2025
position_end: A flat FCFA 100 charged by retail agents on every deposit or withdrawal regardless of amount, on top of roughly 1% operator pricing on withdrawals
note: no operator tariff or regulator authorises it and the regulator's position is not on file

subject: dpi.pay
name: Regional instant-payment interoperability mandate
milestone: Made mandatory from 2026-06-30 by a communique of 2 April 2026
position_start: Did not exist as an obligation
position_end: Instant-payment interoperability compulsory across the monetary union for banks, microfinance institutions, electronic-money institutions and payment institutions
note: no account of Ivorian institutions' compliance after the deadline is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: School-fee collection over mobile money
milestone: Convention signed 2026-07-21, pilot from August 2026
position_end: Pilot in 200 private secular schools: fee collection through a mobile wallet, credit lines to schools and fee pre-financing for parents up to FCFA 1 million
note: no fee volume, pilot duration, pricing or data-handling arrangement disclosed

subject: dpi.pay
name: Treasury payments platform
milestone: Extension toward local authorities reported
position_start: In operation for public-expenditure and government-to-person flows, with the expenditure module under optimisation
position_end: Extended toward local authorities, with 75 collectivities and 4,500 distributors claimed
note: the 2026 figures come from the developer's own press note

subject: dpi.pay
name: Yango and AFG Holding financial-services agreement
milestone: Protocole d'accord signed in Abidjan 2026-08-04
position_end: Signed intention between the ride-hailing platform's Ivorian arm and a fifteen-market banking group, with insurance as the first phase and fleet financing and further digital financial services named as later tracks, and Cote d'Ivoire stated by both parties as the pilot market before replication elsewhere
note: no amount, facility or timetable is stated by either party

subject: dpi.registry
name: Biometric electoral register
milestone: Definitive 2025 list closed by the electoral commission 2 June 2025
position_end: The definitive electoral list was closed by the electoral commission's central commission on 2 June 2025, following the revision of 19 October to 17 November 2024 under decret 2024-792, deletion of the deceased and of those stripped of civil rights on lists supplied by the justice and interior ministries, and a public audit of the provisional list; the commission states that residual imperfections are neutralised by the register's biometrics
note: the release states no enrolment total

subject: dpi.registry
name: Civil-registry software rollout
milestone: 283 birth-registration terminals handed to health workers in the Tonkpi region, 2026-08-11
position_start: Partial rollout, with the interior ministry calling for deployment to be accelerated
position_end: Installed with hardware in every municipal and sub-prefecture civil-status centre for digital recording of births, marriages and deaths, financed by the European Union; the national civil-status system now covers 699 centres and has digitised more than four million records, and on 11 August 2026 the identification office handed 283 digital birth-registration terminals to health workers in the Tonkpi region to link maternities directly to civil-registry offices under a zero-invisible-child programme
note: the centre count, record count and terminal figures are the identification office's own; no registration-rate outcome is attached to them

subject: dpi.registry
name: Digital birth-registration terminals
milestone: Presented at the African civil registration day 2026-08-11
position_end: Terminals for systematic birth registration in service, on which a parent's national identity card populates the child's identity data directly, presented by the civil-registry office at the ninth African civil registration day
note: the claim to be the first in West Africa to use the technology for systematic birth registration is the registry office's own; no deployment count or registration figure is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: e-mining cadastre portal
milestone: Inaugurated 2025-09-22
position_end: Full mining-title cycle online, hosted on secure cloud, with more than 200 mining officials trained
note: no dataset has been published out of the cadastre and nothing since launch reports permits processed

subject: dpi.registry
name: Electronic rural land certificates under PRESFOR
milestone: First five certificates signed electronically at Bongouanou 12 March 2026
position_end: The country's first electronic rural land certificates - five of them, validated by the sub-prefectural committee - signed by the prefect of the Moronou region at Bongouanou on 12 March 2026 under the rural land tenure security programme PRESFOR
note: the base does not state whether the programme issues through SIFOR-CI

subject: dpi.registry
name: IDUFCI unique land identifier
milestone: Instituted by decret n 2019-221 of 13 March 2019
position_start: Instituted by decret n 2019-221 of 13 March 2019 as the single identifier of an Ivorian parcel, carried alongside SIGFU in urban land management
position_end: Instituted by decret n 2019-221 of 13 March 2019 as the single identifier of an Ivorian parcel, carried alongside SIGFU in urban land management
note: the base holds no figure for how many parcels carry the identifier

subject: dpi.registry
name: On-time birth registration rate
milestone: 2024 yearbook presented 2025-06-30
position_end: The same figure, still the latest published
note: no 2025 yearbook is held, so the falling trend has not been updated in over a year

subject: dpi.registry
name: SIFOR-CI rural land information system
milestone: Created by ordonnance n 2025-85 of 12 February 2025
position_start: Created by ordonnance n 2025-85 of 12 February 2025, which sets its remit, organisation and operation as the information system of Ivorian rural land
position_end: Created by ordonnance n 2025-85 of 12 February 2025, which sets its remit, organisation and operation as the information system of Ivorian rural land
note: nothing on file since the creating ordinance on what has been built

subject: dpi.registry
name: SIGFU integrated urban land management system
milestone: Created by decret n 2021-862 of 15 December 2021
position_start: Created by decret n 2021-862 of 15 December 2021 as the integrated system for spatial and textual urban land data, intended to automate the processing circuit of administrative acts end to end
position_end: Operating as the central platform on which every land application - definitive concession order, subdivision, transfer - is recorded and tracked in real time, holding each parcel's history and connecting the tax, land and urban-planning administrations, with the construction ministry's SIGNE electronic signature in use since January 2024
note: no published count of parcels or files processed

subject: dpi.mis
name: Agricultural e-voucher and CropScope
milestone: Rollout announced with the agriculture ministry 22 October 2025
position_end: A digital agriculture project with the agriculture ministry, deploying an e-voucher system to identify and register farmers and distribute seed and fertiliser equitably, alongside the CropScope crop-management platform to stabilise and predict harvests
note: vendor announcement; no enrolment or coverage figure published

subject: dpi.mis
name: Digital national school map
milestone: Education-sector stakeholders convened at Yamoussoukro, 19 August 2026
position_end: Work has begun to digitise the national school map by building geographic information systems onto the integrated education management information system; no coverage, timetable or delivery date is on file

subject: dpi.mis
name: National digital health platform
milestone: Acceptance surveyed among community and frontline health workers, May 2026
position_start: Outbreak surveillance ran across several separate systems, whose characteristics and reception among users were surveyed in July 2024
position_end: A national digital health platform is in use, with a cross-sectional study of May 2026 finding acceptance differing between community and frontline health workers; mHealth and DHIS2 interoperability work was reported in September 2025
note: the base holds research on the platform rather than a ministry statement of its scope

subject: dpi.mis
name: SIGE education management information system
milestone: Handed over to the education ministry 10 July 2025
position_end: The national education management information system was handed to the education ministry on 10 July 2025, financed under the Millennium Challenge Corporation's Skills for Employability and Productivity programme and piloted in the Bouake and San Pedro regions, to carry enrolment tracking, school-building planning, staff and materiel allocation and dropout monitoring; the minister used the handover to appeal for financing to take it national
note: national rollout was unfunded at handover

subject: dpi.mis
name: SIMT labour market information system
milestone: Launched 23 June 2026
position_end: Launched on 23 June 2026, an SDMX-compliant platform run by the national employment and training observatory carrying 134 of an identified 315 indicators across 14 themes, 91 of them published in 299 statistical tables disaggregated by sex, age, education, residence and region, built with ILO technical support and World Bank financing

subject: dpi.mis
name: Transport data platform
milestone: Handed over 2026-04-15
position_end: Collects and analyses road, port, airport and rail flow data, with corridor and checkpoint mapping and decision dashboards

subject: dpi.mis
name: Universal health insurance number as single patient identifier
milestone: Decree adopted by the Council of Ministers 10 July 2024
position_end: A decree adopted on 10 July 2024 makes the Couverture maladie universelle registration number the single patient identifier in every public and private health facility, replacing any other number used to open a record, deliver care or reference a patient's health data, with twenty-four months given to bring hospital information systems into conformity
note: the conformity deadline fell in July 2026; nothing on file reports compliance

subject: dpi.mis
name: Urban video-protection system
milestone: Stated complete across the 12 police prefectures in the 2011-2025 record
position_end: The government's 2011-2025 security record states that all 12 police prefectures and the strategic towns are covered by the urban video-protection system
note: a government self-report; no camera count or independent verification on file

subject: dpi.govtech
name: CERTINUM data-protection compliance platform
milestone: Presented to the insurance sector 2026-08-17, after banking and financial institutions
position_start: Did not exist; compliance and authorisation files handled on paper at about a hundred a month
position_end: Live, with online submission, real-time tracking and traceability for personal-data conformity, processing authorisations and video-surveillance authorisations; the regulator is running a sector-by-sector rollout, having covered banking and financial institutions and then presented the platform to insurers at their association's headquarters, and its communique of 3 August directs all data controllers, data-protection correspondents and advisory firms onto it
note: no post-launch throughput figure has been published, and no cut-off for paper filings, compliance deadline or fee schedule is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital driving licence
milestone: Accepted at roadside checks as at May 2026
position_start: The transport directorate published its list of invalidated licences online on 18 July 2025 under arrete n 0017 of 5 June 2025, opening it to roadside police checks, and opened a points-recovery centre issuing points-balance statements
position_end: The licence is carried on a phone through the CGI Digital application, built under a transport-ministry partnership with Quipux Afrique, showing the licence and its points balance in real time and accepted at roadside checks where officers scan it against the central database, with renewals, video-enforcement fines and carte grise handled through the eservices.cgi.ci portal; drivers are still advised to carry the physical card

subject: dpi.govtech
name: e-Justice platform
milestone: Last eleven tribunals connected 2026-06-29
position_end: All 39 first-instance tribunals connected, with nationality certificates and criminal-record extracts issued nationwide
note: the January 2025 pilot ran in two jurisdictions, Dabou and Yopougon; described as completing phase one, with no phase-two scope or date

subject: dpi.govtech
name: EMY 101 government AI assistant
milestone: Launched 2026-03-18
position_end: Live on messaging platforms and a toll-free line, covering civil status, tax and ministerial guidance and a citizen reporting channel
note: no usage, accuracy, cost, vendor or underlying model has been published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Government electronic-signature programme
milestone: Commerce ministry leadership enrolment began 2026-08-12
position_end: Rolling out across the administration under the public service and administrative modernisation ministry, already covering the civil service, the tax administration and the construction and mining ministries, with the commerce, industry and artisanal craft ministry beginning to enrol its leadership on 12 August 2026
note: no certificate authority, standard, enrolment total or legal-effect statement is held for the programme

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Government software licence appropriation
milestone: Voted FCFA 4.40bn in the 2026 finance law
position_end: FCFA 4,400,000,000 for FY2026, up 49% year on year and 116% over three years
note: the only line in this corpus where the budget names its supplier

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Government website reference template
milestone: Presented to institutional IT and communication directors 2026-07-30
position_end: Reference model for institutional websites developed by the government information and communication centre with technical support from the national development-informatics company, available in six languages and imposing a common graphic, technical and editorial frame on public sites; no adoption instrument, compliance obligation or count of sites using it is stated
note: escalation for a compromised institutional site or a fake institutional account runs to the communication centre, the informatics company or the cyber agency

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Ivoire GovTech Lab
milestone: Launched 2026-07-29
position_end: Launched on 29 July 2026 to publish government digitalisation projects for direct bidding by start-ups and small firms, alongside applications opening for two 30-company digital-sector support programmes and a 2026-2028 ministry roadmap naming artificial-intelligence adoption among seven strategic pillars
note: no project list, budget or award record for the lab is published, and the roadmap text is not held

subject: tech.ai
name: AI acceleration programme
milestone: Launched alongside the strategy handover, 2025-03-13
position_start: Development-bank-supported programme of about FCFA 49bn including a data centre
position_end: Same scope; named in May 2026 as one of the structures that would assess a vendor's public-administration proposals, with no disbursement, milestone or completion figure

subject: tech.ai
name: AI strategy financing
milestone: Costed at FCFA 912bn over five years, February 2025
position_start: Costing with no appropriation identified against it
position_end: Unchanged; no AI-specific line is identifiable in the FY2025 or FY2026 finance laws the wiki holds
note: an AI budget line, or a disbursement record for the acceleration programme, would settle it

subject: tech.ai
name: Francophone West African AI governance guidelines
milestone: Adopted and announced 2026-07-06
position_end: Common guidelines adopted by six states on transparent and inclusive AI, data protection, algorithmic-bias mitigation and digital sovereignty, complementing rather than replacing national strategies
note: led by an advocacy organisation, not by a regional body

subject: tech.ai
name: National AI agency
milestone: Ministry states it is being established, 2025-07-01
position_start: The ministry's transformation director says work is under way to establish a national AI agency
position_end: Unchanged; no decree, name, budget or staffing in any held source thirteen months later
note: the coordination role has meanwhile been taken up in practice by the cyber agency through the draft cybersecurity strategy

subject: tech.ai
name: National AI Strategy
status: Implemented, no adoption instrument on file
milestone: Handed to the Prime Minister 2025-03-13
position_start: Handed to the Prime Minister for government adoption, costed at FCFA 912bn with 15 objectives and 109 projects over five years
position_end: Counted among Africa's adopted national AI strategies, with six senior implementation posts advertised from 2026-05-26
note: no Council of Ministers adoption date or decree is on file, and the strategy text is not held

subject: tech.ai
name: National Committee for AI and Data Governance
milestone: Named as an initial action of the AI strategy
position_start: Named as one of the strategy's first actions
position_end: Unchanged; no constitution, membership, chair or meeting on record
note: a creation decree or a first communique would settle whether it exists

subject: tech.ai
name: National Data Governance Strategy 2030
status: Implemented, no adoption instrument on file
milestone: Handed to the Prime Minister 2025-03-13 with the AI strategy
position_start: Handed to the Prime Minister; presented to the private sector May 2025
position_end: Named as one of the two strategies the ministry's six new senior posts exist to implement
note: the strategy document itself is not held

subject: tech.ai
name: National sovereign cloud
milestone: Named as under construction, 2026-04-29
position_start: Provided for in the national AI strategy as a first-pillar investment, with nothing on record being built
position_end: The minister describes a foundation under construction comprising a national data centre at Grand-Bassam, a second project at Yamoussoukro and a sovereign-cloud network; no operator, capacity, cost or commissioning date

subject: tech.ai
name: Public AI university
milestone: Provided for in the 2026-2030 national development plan
position_end: Public university dedicated to artificial intelligence provided for in the development plan, alongside centres of excellence in universities; no site, budget line, intake or date
note: the March 2025 strategy provided for a training centre, not a university

subject: tech.ai
name: Safe AI label
milestone: Provided for in the AI strategy, 2025-03-13
position_start: Named in the national AI strategy as its legal and ethical labelling instrument
position_end: Unchanged; no criteria, awarding body, register or labelled solution on file seventeen months later
note: nothing in any held source mentions it after March 2025

subject: tech.ai
name: SODEXAM and China Meteorological Administration memorandum
milestone: Memorandum signed at Shanghai, reported 2026-08-06
position_end: Six cooperation axes covering intelligent numerical forecasting adapted to Ivorian conditions, a next-generation early-warning system built on cloud and artificial intelligence, metrological capacity-building, joint monsoon research, extension of early-warning coverage to the most vulnerable populations and continued training; the state airport and meteorological operator separately requested a US$21m grant (2026) from the Chinese government for an artificial-intelligence multi-hazard early-warning deployment, which nothing on file establishes has been agreed
note: a March 2023 donation of media-studio equipment valued at US$106,560 brought Feng Yun satellite data into the operator's forecasting tools; neither the memorandum nor the request is reported to address where the data sits or the terms of continued access

subject: tech.industry
name: Electric ride-hailing fleet
milestone: 100 vehicles delivered 2026-07-18
position_end: 100 fully electric vehicles handed to ride-hailing driver-partners, the first half of a 200-vehicle programme on drive-to-own repayment over three years
note: the operator's energy-cost benchmarks are its own and unverified

subject: tech.industry
name: National industry 4.0 strategy
milestone: Handed to government 2025-02-26
position_start: Strategy handed to the commerce and industry minister, developed with UN industrial-development support on German funding
position_end: Unchanged; no adoption, budget, implementing body or activity on file seventeen months later
note: the only industrial-technology strategy instrument the wiki holds for this country

subject: tech.innovate
name: E-tourism platform
milestone: Roadmap presented April 2026, partnership confirmed at the 2026 national tourism council
position_end: One-stop gateway for discovery, itinerary planning and booking, built for the tourism ministry by the same US vendor as the national data centre; no cost, launch date or contract value

subject: tech.innovate
name: Government technology procurement platform
milestone: Unveiled 2026-07-29
position_end: Platform on which the state's own digital-transformation projects are to be published for startups and small firms to bid directly; nothing establishes it is live or that any project has been published
note: the demand-side instrument in the package, and the part that would move money

subject: tech.innovate
name: Ministerial digital roadmap 2026-2028
milestone: Presented at African Digital Week June 2026 and to the ITU 2026-07-08
position_start: Did not exist; the 2021-2025 national digital development strategy was the instrument in force and expiring
position_end: Ministerial roadmap in force on seven pillars and 40 priority projects, sitting under the national digital development strategy and the 2026-2030 development plan
note: the roadmap text is not held; the pillar and project counts are ministry-sourced press claims

subject: tech.innovate
name: Startup accelerator cohorts
milestone: Launched 2026-07-29, applications close 2026-09-13
position_end: Two cohorts of fifteen, one of trading startups and one of digital small and medium enterprises, each accompanied for 24 months, against a stated target of FCFA 5 to 10bn mobilised from banks, funds and donors
note: the mobilisation figure is an ambition, not committed capital

subject: tech.innovate
name: Startup Act and digital startup label
milestone: Adopted November 2023
position_start: Startup Act adopted with a digital startup label, fiscal and customs incentives and a national labelling committee
position_end: Unchanged; no count of labelled startups, no implementing decree, no evaluation and no reported use of the public-procurement route

subject: tech.innovate
name: Startup funding raised
milestone: Tracker report for 2025 published 2026-02-03
position_start: US$4,717,000 across four funded ventures in 2024
position_end: US$17,920,000 across three funded ventures in 2025, up 280%, of which financial technology took US$17,000,000
note: a tracker whose methodology books undisclosed rounds at the lowest possible figure, so the totals are floors

subject: tech.innovate
name: Technological Innovation Fund
milestone: Announced at the July 2025 technology forum with a six-month mobilisation pledge
position_start: Announced at FCFA 100bn with nothing capitalised and a six-month mobilisation window running
position_end: Unchanged; no capitalisation, manager, governance, first close or disbursement on file, and the window closed in January 2026
note: the two held accounts disagree on whether it was launched or only appealed for

subject: tech.innovate
name: UniPod innovation and technology hub
milestone: Handed over at the Lycee technique de Cocody during the 8 to 13 July 2026 visit, reported 2026-08-04
position_end: The country's first digital-fabrication laboratory, sited in a public technical school with the national education ministry as contracting authority and running 16 functional zones across five poles equipped to Fab Academy standards; total project cost put at over FCFA 800m (2026), with no per-financier split, operating budget, sustainment funding or replication timetable stated
note: access is stated to target 50% women; the cost is a project total across the UN development programme, Japan, the African Development Bank, the World Bank and Ivorian public and private institutions

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Birth-declaration rate
milestone: Identification office director general's statement
position_end: Below 60%, against a stated near-universal ambition
note: a dated statement with no published series behind it

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Education digitalisation baseline study
milestone: Technical validation of tools, December 2025
position_start: Did not exist; work began October 2025
position_end: Conceptual framework, sampling plan and collection tools technically validated, awaiting ministerial validation before national collection
note: eight months on, no source establishes the national collection was launched or any result published

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Innovation and culture centres in schools
milestone: Nine centres open, twenty announced for 2026
position_end: Nine centres operating in interior schools, with twenty more announced for 2026
note: first count on file is June 2026; no opening dates, cost or usage figures

subject: capacity.literacy
name: National education digitalisation project
milestone: Six of eight components completed; technical and financial agreement unsigned
position_end: Six of eight components complete, with the agreement still to be signed
note: no cost, financier or component list published; the project is described only by its stage count

subject: capacity.literacy
name: National-language civil-registration relays
milestone: Capacity-building seminar, Abidjan, 2026-06-09
position_end: National-language announcers trained as community relays on civil registration and the identification number, with community collection points to follow
note: no number of speakers trained, budget or geographic coverage stated

subject: capacity.training
name: Certified cyber-specialist programme
milestone: Target of 1,200 certified in three years announced 2026-07-29
position_end: About 250 trained in the first half of 2026 plus 88 auditors certified, against 500 by year-end and 1,200 in three years
note: the continental expert deficit the director general cites carries no source

subject: capacity.training
name: Chinese digital education loan
milestone: Loan agreements signed 2018-08-31, fully disbursed by December 2022
position_start: Fully disbursed with a Chinese vendor contracted to the education ministry
position_end: Unchanged; no disbursement, completion or evaluation update since December 2022
note: the largest skills-adjacent loan on file and the least reported on

subject: capacity.training
name: Civil-service digital-skills programme
milestone: Thirteenth edition closed at Katiola 2026-07-29
position_end: 192 officials from about thirty public bodies trained over 40 days, against a cumulative claim of more than 37,500 civil servants
note: funded from the ministry's own budget line rather than a donor project; the cumulative figure is undated as to programme start

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital skills programme with a US vendor
milestone: Second annual Cote d'Ivoire summer tech camp closed, hundreds trained across 20 cities, reported 2026-08-11
position_end: Second annual summer tech camp concluded under the Africa DigiEmpower programme, training hundreds of young people in AI, cybersecurity and digital awareness across 20 Ivorian cities; no cumulative headcount published
note: no cumulative figure published since September 2025

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital-skills memorandum with the UN development programme
milestone: Memorandum signed 2026-05-21
position_end: Training, startup support and rural and vulnerable-population outreach through a vendor digital centre
note: no budget, headcount target or duration disclosed by either party

subject: capacity.training
name: Education management information system compact
milestone: Compact closed August 2025
position_end: Compact closed, with no successor operation, outturn or system-status report on file
note: the consultancy component leaves no published closing evaluation

subject: capacity.training
name: National digital-skills headcount
milestone: No reconciled national figure exists
note: each programme publishes its own cumulative claim and nothing reconciles them

subject: capacity.training
name: Tech Talent Accelerator
milestone: Cohort closed with 51 projects presented 2026-08-04
position_end: A German-funded three-month cohort closing with 51 artificial-intelligence projects across finance, health, law, education and cybersecurity; participant numbers, cost and what becomes of the projects are not stated
note: the count of projects is the only published measure of the programme, and a project unveiled at a demonstration day is not evidence of a deployed system

subject: capacity.training
name: Vocational teacher-training institute ICT programme
milestone: Facilities handed over and training begun 2026-08-18
position_end: Practical-training facilities at the national vocational teacher-training institute remodelled, equipped and handed over by a Korean university, with ICT capacity training begun for 1,280 local teachers under a donor country programme running 2022-2027 covering 1,000 teachers in ICT and pedagogy, 200 across four engineering specialisms and 80 institute master teachers
note: 78 vocational teachers completed the in-country training, on the delivering university's own account

subject: capacity.research
name: Cyber-security masters degrees
milestone: Curricula examined and validated at the 2026-07-28 workshop
position_end: Two degrees, in information-systems security and digital forensics, with enrolment stated for the September 2026 academic year
note: no intake size or funding stated

subject: capacity.research
name: Higher school for information and communication technologies
milestone: Institutional presentation held
position_end: A public higher school for information and communication technologies, held through its own evergreen institutional presentation
note: the page carries no publication date of its own, so nothing here may be dated to a development; no enrolment, graduation or placement figure is published

subject: include.access
name: Civil-registry agency in a shopping centre
milestone: Opened at Yopougon 2026-08-14
position_end: A civil-registry and identification agency opened inside a Yopougon shopping centre in partnership with a private mobility company, presented as bringing identification services closer to citizens
